citation: Gheibi, Yeganeh Khaksar and Hoshyar (2026), EnerTwin: A Digital Twin Software for Occupancy-Driven Building Energy and Sustainability Analysis, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21441078
description: EnerTwin is a small digital twin application for analysing how occupancy affects a building's energy demand, operating cost and carbon emissions. It was published on Zenodo on 19 July 2026 by Mohammad Gheibi of the Technical University of Liberec, Reza Yeganeh Khaksar of Aalto University and Amirhossein Hoshyar. Through a graphical interface it combines occupancy-based demand modelling, end-use analysis, fuel allocation, photovoltaic generation, economic evaluation and greenhouse gas accounting, and runs scenarios with key performance indicators and sensitivity analysis for researchers, energy managers, consultants and facility operators. Coverage: a single building defined by the user. Access: one MATLAB file (EnerTwin.m) on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free, though MATLAB is commercial. Caveats: a new single-file tool with no documentation beyond the record; not a physics-based simulation engine. Simulation uses are quick occupancy and PV scenario screening for building operation and emissions. Related records: BuildOcc and the D^2EPC digital twin data model.
